turns.prompt_text: My vape is not working it has enough juice in it and it is charged It is just not creating the vapor Attached 1 file. - 421d8874-ce19-4480-be4d-606df79763d4
turns.response_html:
The Geekvape Sonder relies on a draw-activation sensor and magnetic contact pins inside the battery slot. If the LED doesn't light up when you inhale, or blinks without firing, work through these steps to fix the connection:

  • Clean the Contact Pins: Pull the pod out. Look inside the well for the two gold contact pins and the small airflow hole. E-liquid or condensation frequently leaks onto these contacts and prevents electrical connection. Thoroughly wipe down the bottom of the pod and inside the cavity with a Q-tip or tissue (optionally dabbed with a drop of isopropyl alcohol).
  • Check the Draw Sensor: If the LED doesn't light up when you inhale, the draw sensor inside the well may be clogged with liquid. Remove the pod, place a paper towel over the top cavity, and blow firmly into the USB-C charge port on the bottom or side to push any trapped liquid out of the sensor.
  • Inspect the Spring Pins: Look inside the chamber to ensure both spring-loaded pins bounce back up. If one pin is stuck recessed inside the casing, gently tap the device or use a toothpick to tease it back up.
  • Check for Protective Film: If this is a brand-new pod, make sure the clear plastic sticker covering the bottom connection contacts was removed before inserting.
  • Try a Replacement Pod: If the LED blinks (typically 3 or 5 times) when you draw, the device detects an open circuit or burned-out coil, meaning the internal coil wire in that pod has broken and the pod needs replacement.

If the LED still does not light up at all when inhaling, cover the small side airflow intake hole slightly with a finger while drawing to create stronger suction to trip the sensor.

turns.prompt_text: The LED does slowly become bright enough when I inhale
turns.response_html:
If the LED slowly "breathes" or brightens when you take a puff, the draw-activation sensor is working properly and telling the chip to fire, but current isn't heating the coil.

  • The Coil is Burnt or Has an Open Circuit: If the heating element inside the pod has snapped or severed, the device thinks it is firing, but current cannot complete the circuit to heat up the juice. Swapping in a fresh Sonder U-pod will resolve this.
  • Insufficient Pin Pressure/Contact: A microscopic film of condensed juice or a stuck spring pin can allow the draw sensor to activate while creating too much electrical resistance for the actual heating current.
    • Remove the pod and use a dry cotton swab to vigorously clean the two bottom metal discs on the pod and the two spring pins inside the slot.
    • Push each gold pin down with a toothpick to make sure both spring fully back up.
  • Low Battery Voltage Under Load: If the battery is nearly depleted, it might have enough voltage to trigger the LED animation, but will instantly drop voltage and fail to power the heating coil when under load. Plug it into a standard 5V wall block for 30 minutes to ensure a solid charge.
  • Severely Flooded Coil: If the pod's chimney and core are drowned in juice, the coil can't heat up enough liquid to vaporize it. Remove the pod, wrap the base in a paper towel, and blow hard downward through the mouthpiece to clear any excess pooling liquid before reinserting.
